problem: Is the function $f(x,y,z)=2xyz-{y}^{3}+{y}^{2}z$ homogeneous? If so, what is its degree?
worked_solution:
A function $f(x,y,z)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
f(tx,ty,tz)={t}^{n}f(x,y,z).
$$

So first, we compute $f(tx,ty,tz),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}f(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(tx,ty,tz) & =2(tx)(ty)(tz)-(ty)^{3}+(ty)^{2}(tz) \\  & =2{t}^{3}xyz-{t}^{3}{y}^{3}+{t}^{3}{y}^{2}z \\  & ={t}^{3}(2xyz-{y}^{3}+{y}^{2}z) \\  & ={t}^{3}f(x,y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
f(tx,ty,tz)={t}^{3}f(x,y,z)
$$

and so the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y,z)$ is $3.$
